_format: skill-creator eval format — see https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/evaluating-skills. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions.

evals.prompt: Write me a skill that teaches the agent our staging deploy procedure: build, push to registry, bump the kustomize tag, wait for argo sync, smoke-test.
assertions: Creates skills/<kebab-name>/SKILL.md (or .claude/skills/...) with frontmatter name equal to the directory name
Description states what the skill does plus 'Use when' trigger phrases, third person, under 1024 chars
Body leads with the decision/procedure, imperative voice, no Overview/Introduction section
Fragile exact-sequence steps are specific (low degrees of freedom): exact commands, no alternative-tool menus
Rarely-needed detail is split to a sibling reference file, linked one level deep

evals.prompt: My kubernetes-debugging skill never fires when I ask things like 'why is this pod crashlooping' — it only fires if I literally say kubernetes. Fix it.
assertions: Diagnoses the description as the trigger surface and edits it (not the body) to add symptom phrasings like crashloop/pod/OOM
Keeps description within budget (1024 spec cap; 1536 listing cap) and checks nothing else gets squeezed out
Recommends probing with realistic symptom phrasings, not only canonical ones

evals.prompt: I want the agent to always use conventional commits in this repo. Should that be a skill?
assertions: Routes an always-on project rule to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, not a skill
Explains the cost model briefly: skill bodies load on trigger, CLAUDE.md is always-on
Does not create an unnecessary skill
